findings.text:
What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)
The right inner speech can be absent: "They do not say in their hearts, 'Let us fear the Lord'"
Scripture speaks back into inner speech. It forbids it ("Do not say in your heart", Deu 9:4; "Beware lest you say", 8:17) and answers it (Deu 7:17–18; 18:21–22)

Inner speech leads to deed:
• David "said in his heart" and fled (1Sa 27:1)
• Jeroboam "said in his heart" and made the calves (1Ki 12:26–28)
• Esau planned murder (Gen 27:41)
• Haman's self-talk (Est 6:6)
What is said outwardly and what the heart holds can differ ("inwardly calculating … his heart is not with you")

God hears what goes out, both ways: the enemies' plots ("You have heard their taunts … all their plots", Lam 3:61) and the talk of those who fear him ("The Lord paid attention and heard them", Mal 3:16). This is outbound hearing. Refusing to listen goes with devising. (The discussion cited Mal 3:16 under "plots"; corrected here.) The researcher's words: "hearing is an integral part of the outbound thought"
Love reckons as God reckons: love is "not resentful" (does not count wrong), as God is "not counting their trespasses"; "may it not be charged against them"

Job 42:7 says Job spoke rightly; this reading is still not God's own word about Job (R; crosses into the anger strand)

Face: God's reckoning of man and nations; Verses: Isa 40:15, 17; Psa 144:3; 40:17; Isa 2:22; What differs: God counts nations as dust, and yet "takes thought for me"; Why (basis): The same God reckons great powers as nothing and the poor as worth his thought (S)

Turned on others' forgetting: "think to make my people forget my name by their dreams" (Jer 23:27); Why (basis): Where the thinking is done changes what it can see (S)

Face: God devising against, conditionally; Verses: Jer 18:8, 11; 26:3; 36:3; Mic 2:3; Jer 49:20, 30; 50:45; Lam 2:8; What differs: God devises "against", but: "Return, every one from his evil way" (18:11); "It may be they will listen … that I may relent of the disaster that I intend" (26:3); Why (basis): God's "against" is aimed at turning, and it is open to change. "Against" alone does not make thinking evil (S)

Face: God devising for; Verses: Jer 29:11; 2Sa 14:14; Gen 50:20b; What differs: "plans for welfare and not for evil" (Jer 29:11); "he devises means so that the banished one will not remain an outcast" (2Sa 14:14); Why (basis): For whom God thinks: the exile, the banished (S)
Thoughts to be forsaken: "let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts" (Isa 55:7). The next line gives the answer: "for he will abundantly pardon".
Own devices against God's outstretched hands: "I spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own devices" (Isa 65:2).
Pure words against impure thoughts: "The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord, but gracious words are pure" (Pro 15:26).
The crafty frustrated: "He frustrates the devices of the crafty … He catches the wise in their own craftiness" (Job 5:12–13; 5:13 read as context).
Multiplying thoughts, toward us: "your thoughts toward us; none can compare with you" (Psa 40:5).

What changes it: whose thought it is, toward or against whom, whether counsel is taken, haste or diligence. Jer 18:11–18 holds three faces in one passage (proposal §2.2). Jer 18:8 makes God's face conditional.

Quick temper and evil devices in one proverb: "A man of quick temper acts foolishly, and a man of evil devices is hated" (Pro 14:17). Temper and scheming are set side by side. This is a link to the anger strand.

God's purpose is carried by his anger: "The anger of the Lord will not turn back until he has executed and accomplished the intents of his heart. In the latter days you will understand it clearly" (Jer 23:20; 30:24). The word for discretion and for evil device is here God's *intent*, and his anger serves it. Understanding comes only afterwards. This is a link to the anger strand.
